q-idiom-meaning.label: Meaning of an idiom
q-idiom-meaning.summary: An idiom in inverted commas; pick the option that gives its meaning.

rules.text: An idiom means something different from its words put together. Never choose the option that restates the literal picture.
rules.ok: Spill the beans = reveal a secret.
rules.bad: Spill the beans = drop some beans.

q-idiom-meaning.cue: 'Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom/phrase' with the idiom in inverted commas.
q-idiom-meaning.standard: Recall the meaning as a unit, then match it. If you do not know it, work out the feeling the idiom carries (good, bad, secret, effort) from the sentence it came from.
q-idiom-meaning.fast: Drop any option that is the literal reading, then match the remaining ones by feeling.
q-idiom-meaning.eliminate: Other idioms' meanings are usually the wrong options; if you recognise one of them as belonging to a different idiom, cross it out.
traps: The literal meaning is nearly always listed as bait.
The meaning of a similar-sounding idiom is the second common trap.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
'spill the beans'
options: To work or study late into the night
To reveal a secret
To drop food while cooking
Very rarely
practice.why: To spill the beans is to reveal a secret.

a.note: That is the meaning of 'burn the midnight oil', a different idiom.

c.note: This is the literal reading of the words; an idiom never means its literal picture.

d.note: That is the meaning of 'once in a blue moon'; it has nothing to do with secrets.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
'a blessing in disguise'
options: To be extremely expensive
To state exactly what is true or right
A misfortune that turns out to be beneficial
A prayer said quietly
practice.why: A blessing in disguise is a misfortune that turns out to be beneficial.

a.note: That is the meaning of 'cost an arm and a leg'.

b.note: That is the meaning of 'hit the nail on the head'.

d.note: This takes 'blessing' and 'disguise' literally; the idiom is about luck in the end.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
'once in a blue moon'
options: Very rarely
On the night of a full moon
To ease the awkwardness among people meeting for the first time
To face a painful or difficult situation with courage
practice.why: Once in a blue moon means very rarely.

b.note: This reads 'blue moon' as the moon itself; the idiom is about how seldom something happens.

c.note: That is the meaning of 'break the ice'.

d.note: That is the meaning of 'bite the bullet'.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
'bite the bullet'
options: To reveal a secret
To face a painful or difficult situation with courage
To chew something hard
A misfortune that turns out to be beneficial
practice.why: To bite the bullet is to face a painful situation with courage.

a.note: That is the meaning of 'spill the beans'.

c.note: This is the literal picture of biting; the idiom means enduring something hard.

d.note: That is the meaning of 'a blessing in disguise'.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
'hit the nail on the head'
options: To work or study late into the night
To state exactly what is true or right
To strike a nail with a hammer
To be extremely expensive
practice.why: To hit the nail on the head is to state exactly what is true or right.

a.note: That is the meaning of 'burn the midnight oil'.

c.note: This is the literal reading; the idiom is about being exactly right.

d.note: That is the meaning of 'cost an arm and a leg'.

practice.text:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
'cost an arm and a leg'
options: To be injured badly
To ease the awkwardness among people meeting for the first time
A misfortune that turns out to be beneficial
To be extremely expensive
practice.why: To cost an arm and a leg is to be extremely expensive.

a.note: This reads the body parts literally; the idiom is about price.

b.note: That is the meaning of 'break the ice'.

c.note: That is the meaning of 'a blessing in disguise'.
